# VERCEL_DEPLOY.md

# Vercel Deployment Checklist
## Expo Router v5 + Clerk + Supabase

---

## 0. Prerequisites

- [ ] Vercel account with access to the target team/org
- [ ] Vercel CLI installed globally: `npm i -g vercel@latest`
- [ ] Logged in: `vercel login`
- [ ] Production domain decided (e.g. `app.yourdomain.com`) — you need this BEFORE
      configuring Clerk and Supabase allowed origins
- [ ] All secrets available:
  - `pk_live_*` Clerk publishable key (switch from `pk_test_*` for production)
  - `sk_live_*` Clerk secret key
  - Supabase project URL + anon key + service role key
  - Any other API keys used in API routes

---

## 1. Pre-Deployment: Code Fixes

### 1.1 Fix Clerk token-cache — native-only import

`@clerk/expo/token-cache` calls `expo-secure-store` which is not available on web.
Wrap it with a Platform guard wherever `tokenCache` is passed to `<ClerkProvider>`.

Edit your root layout (e.g. `app/_layout.tsx`):

// app/_layout.tsx
import { Platform } from 'react-native';
import { ClerkProvider } from '@clerk/clerk-expo';

// Only import on native — web uses in-memory / cookie storage automatically
const tokenCache =
  Platform.OS !== 'web'
    ? (() => {
        // Lazy require so the module is never evaluated on web
        const { createTokenCache } = require('@clerk/expo/token-cache');
        return createTokenCache();
      })()
    : undefined;

export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <ClerkProvider
      publishableKey={process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY!}
      tokenCache={tokenCache}   // undefined on web = Clerk uses cookies
    >
      {/* ... */}
    </ClerkProvider>
  );
}

- [ ] Code change committed and pushed to your deployment branch

---

### 1.2 Fix EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL — must be production URL

This env var is baked into the client bundle at build time by Expo.
It MUST point to the production Vercel domain, not `localhost`.

In `.env.local` (local dev only — not committed):
EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:8081/api/secure-proxy

In Vercel dashboard (see §3 below) set:
EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL=https://app.yourdomain.com/api/secure-proxy

- [ ] Confirm `.env.local` is in `.gitignore`
- [ ] Confirm the Vercel env var will use the production value (set in §3.3)

---

### 1.3 Verify API route filename convention

Expo Router SSR API routes must use the `+api.ts` suffix.

- [ ] Confirm file is `app/api/secure-proxy+api.ts`
- [ ] Confirm the file exports at least one of: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`

// app/api/secure-proxy+api.ts — minimal shape check
export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  // ...
}

---

### 1.4 Confirm web.output = "server" in app.json / app.config.ts

{
  "expo": {
    "web": {
      "output": "server",
      "bundler": "metro"
    }
  }
}

- [ ] `web.output` is `"server"` (NOT `"static"`)
- [ ] Build produces `dist/server/` and `dist/client/` directories locally:
  npx expo export --platform web
  ls dist/
  # → client/  server/

---

### 1.5 Confirm vercel.json exists at repo root

The correct `vercel.json` for Expo Router v5 with `web.output = "server"` is
more complex than a simple rewrite list. Here is why:

**Why the complex routes are required:**

Expo Router v5 in server-output mode splits the build into two directories:
- `dist/client/` — JS bundles, fonts, images, favicon (static assets)
- `dist/server/` — pre-rendered HTML pages and compiled API route handlers

Critically, **there is no `dist/server/_expo/functions/__root__.js`** in this
output mode. Expo Router pre-renders each route to its own HTML file
(e.g. `dist/server/(tabs)/index.html`). A simple catch-all rewrite pointing to
`__root__.js` will cause every page request to return 404 because that file does
not exist.

The `vercel.json` must therefore:
1. Serve `/_expo/static/**` and `/assets/**` directly from `dist/client/`
2. Route `/api/secure-proxy` to the compiled serverless function in `dist/server/`
3. Map each known page path explicitly to its pre-rendered HTML file in `dist/server/`
4. Fall through to `dist/server/+not-found.html` for unknown routes

{
  "buildCommand": "npx expo export --platform web",
  "outputDirectory": "dist",
  "framework": null,
  "routes": [
    {
      "src": "/_expo/static/(.*)",
      "dest": "/client/_expo/static/$1"
    },
    {
      "src": "/assets/(.*)",
      "dest": "/client/assets/$1"
    },
    {
      "src": "/favicon.ico",
      "dest": "/client/favicon.ico"
    },
    {
      "src": "/api/secure-proxy",
      "dest": "/server/_expo/functions/api/secure-proxy+api.js"
    },
    {
      "src": "/",
      "dest": "/server/(tabs)/index.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/explore",
      "dest": "/server/(tabs)/explore.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/scheduler",
      "dest": "/server/(tabs)/scheduler.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/sign-in",
      "dest": "/server/(auth)/sign-in.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/sign-up",
      "dest": "/server/(auth)/sign-up.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/_sitemap",
      "dest": "/server/_sitemap.html"
    },
    {
      "src": "/(.*)",
      "dest": "/server/+not-found.html"
    }
  ]
}

> **Setting `"framework": null`** overrides any auto-detection. This is equivalent
> to selecting "Other" in the dashboard and prevents Vercel from injecting Next.js
> build logic.
>
> **Do NOT use a simple `"rewrites"` array** pointing to `__root__.js`. That file
> is not produced by Expo Router v5 static-server mode and every page will 404.
>
> **If you add new routes** to the app, add a corresponding entry to the `routes`
> array in `vercel.json` before deploying, otherwise the new page will fall through
> to the `+not-found.html` catch-all.

- [ ] `vercel.json` committed to repo root with the full `routes` array above
- [ ] Every page route in `app/` has a corresponding entry in `vercel.json`
- [ ] No conflicting `next.config.*` file in repo root
- [ ] No simple `"rewrites"` pointing to `__root__.js`

---

### 1.6 Run a local production build and smoke test

npx expo export --platform web
# Should complete with exit code 0 and produce dist/

Verify the expected output structure is present:

ls dist/client/_expo/static/
# → js/  (contains web entry bundle and locale chunk bundles)

ls dist/server/\(tabs\)/
# → index.html  explore.html  scheduler.html

ls dist/server/_expo/functions/api/
# → secure-proxy+api.js

ls dist/server/
# → (tabs)/  (auth)/  _expo/  _sitemap.html  +not-found.html

> **WARNING:** Do NOT look for `dist/server/_expo/functions/__root__.js` — it does
> NOT exist in Expo Router v5 static-server output mode. If you see advice
> referencing that file, it does not apply to this project.

vercel dev          # optional: test serverless functions locally

- [ ] Build exits with code 0
- [ ] `dist/client/_expo/static/` contains JS bundle(s)
- [ ] `dist/server/(tabs)/index.html` exists (pre-rendered home page)
- [ ] `dist/server/_expo/functions/api/secure-proxy+api.js` exists (API handler)
- [ ] `dist/server/+not-found.html` exists (catch-all fallback)
- [ ] No `__root__.js` present (expected — this is correct)

---

## 2. Third-Party Service Configuration

### 2.1 Clerk Dashboard — Add production domain to allowed origins

1. Go to **https://dashboard.clerk.com**
2. Select your application → **Configure** (left sidebar)
3. Navigate to **Domains** → **Allowed Origins**
4. Click **Add origin** and add:

   https://app.yourdomain.com

5. If you are using a Vercel preview URL pattern, also add:

   https://*.vercel.app

   (only if you need preview deployments to work with Clerk)
6. Click **Save**

For production Clerk keys (not test):
- Navigate to **Configure → API Keys**
- Copy the `pk_live_*` publishable key and `sk_live_*` secret key
- [ ] You have the live keys ready for §3.3

- [ ] Production domain added to Clerk allowed origins
- [ ] Live API keys noted for Vercel env vars

---

### 2.2 Supabase Dashboard — Add Vercel domain to CORS allowed origins

1. Go to **https://supabase.com/dashboard**
2. Select your project
3. Navigate to **Project Settings** (gear icon, bottom-left) → **API**
4. Under **CORS allowed origins**, click **Add origin** and enter:

   https://app.yourdomain.com

5. If using Vercel preview deployments:

   https://*.vercel.app

6. Click **Save**

Also verify RLS (Row Level Security):
- Navigate to **Authentication → Policies**
- [ ] Confirm every table accessed from the client has RLS enabled and
      appropriate policies (user can only read/write their own rows)

- [ ] Vercel domain added to Supabase CORS
- [ ] RLS policies reviewed

---

## 3. Vercel Dashboard Configuration

### 3.1 Create / import the project

**New project:**
1. Go to **https://vercel.com/new**
2. Click **Import Git Repository** → select your repo
3. On the "Configure Project" screen — proceed to 3.2 before clicking Deploy

**Existing project — open project settings:**
1. Go to **https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/settings**

---

### 3.2 Set framework to "Other"

In the **Configure Project** screen (or **Settings → General → Framework Preset**):

1. Click the **Framework Preset** dropdown
2. Select **Other**
3. Set **Build Command** to:

   npx expo export --platform web

4. Set **Output Directory** to:

   dist

5. Set **Install Command** to (leave default or set explicitly):

   npm install

6. Set **Node.js Version** to **20.x** (LTS)
   - Path: **Settings → General → Node.js Version**

- [ ] Framework = Other
- [ ] Build command = `npx expo export --platform web`
- [ ] Output directory = `dist`
- [ ] Node.js version = 20.x

---

### 3.3 Set environment variables

Navigate to **Settings → Environment Variables**
(URL: `https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/settings/environment-variables`)

Add ALL of the following. For each:
- Click **Add New**
- Paste the **Name** and **Value**
- Select environments: ✅ Production, ✅ Preview (uncheck Preview for secrets if
  you want isolation), ✅ Development (optional)
- Click **Save**

| Name | Value | Environments |
|------|-------|--------------|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | `pk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx` | Production, Preview |
| `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` | `sk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx` | Production, Preview |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `https://xxxx.supabase.co` | Production, Preview |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `sb_publishable_xxxx` | Production, Preview |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | `sb_secret_xxxx` | Production, Preview |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL` | `https://app.yourdomain.com/api/secure-proxy` | Production |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL` | `https://[your-preview-slug].vercel.app/api/secure-proxy` | Preview |

> **Important:** `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variables are inlined into the client bundle at
> build time. They are NOT secret. Never put secret keys in `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` names.
>
> `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are server-only — they are
> never sent to the browser, only available in API routes / server functions.
>
> `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and any key not in this table) stays in `.env.local` only
> unless your API routes on Vercel need it — if so, add it as Production-only.

- [ ] All env vars added
- [ ] No `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix on secret keys
- [ ] `EXPO_PUBLIC_SECURE_PROXY_URL` set to production domain (not localhost)

---

### 3.4 Assign custom domain

1. Navigate to **Settings → Domains**
   (URL: `https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/settings/domains`)
2. Type `app.yourdomain.com` → click **Add**
3. Vercel shows required DNS records:
   - For apex domain (`yourdomain.com`): **A record** pointing to `76.76.21.21`
   - For subdomain (`app.yourdomain.com`): **CNAME** pointing to `cname.vercel-dns.com`
4. Configure in your DNS provider (see §4)
5. Wait for Vercel to show **Valid Configuration** ✅ and SSL certificate issued

- [ ] Domain added in Vercel dashboard
- [ ] DNS records noted for next step

---

## 4. DNS Configuration

Log in to your DNS provider (Cloudflare, Route53, Namecheap, etc.)

### 4.1 Add DNS records

For a subdomain deployment (`app.yourdomain.com`):

| Type | Name | Value | TTL |
|------|------|-------|-----|
| CNAME | `app` | `cname.vercel-dns.com` | 300 (or Auto) |

For an apex domain (`yourdomain.com`):

| Type | Name | Value | TTL |
|------|------|-------|-----|
| A | `@` | `76.76.21.21` | 300 |

> If using Cloudflare: set the CNAME/A record to **DNS only** (grey cloud) initially
> to avoid SSL conflicts with Vercel's certificate provisioning. You can enable
> the proxy (orange cloud) after the certificate is issued, but you must set
> SSL/TLS mode to **Full (Strict)**.

- [ ] DNS record(s) added
- [ ] Propagation checked: `dig app.yourdomain.com` or https://dnschecker.org
- [ ] Vercel dashboard shows green SSL certificate ✅

---

## 5. Initial Deployment

### 5.1 Trigger deploy

**Via Git (recommended):**
git push origin main        # or your production branch
Vercel auto-deploys on push.

**Via CLI:**
vercel --prod

### 5.2 Monitor the build log

1. Go to **https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/deployments**
2. Click the latest deployment → **Build Logs**
3. Watch for:
   - [ ] `npx expo export --platform web` starts
   - [ ] No missing env var warnings (Expo warns if `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` vars are absent)
   - [ ] `Exporting...` completes successfully
   - [ ] `dist/server/` and `dist/client/` detected by Vercel
   - [ ] Serverless functions detected (look for "Creating Serverless Functions...")
   - [ ] Build status = **Ready** ✅

Common build errors and fixes:

| Error | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `Cannot find module '@clerk/expo/token-cache'` on web build | Apply fix from §1.1 |
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is not defined` | Check §3.3, redeploy |
| `Output directory dist not found` | Check `vercel.json` outputDirectory = `"dist"` |
| Function size limit exceeded | Check for bundled node_modules in API route; use dynamic import |
| Pages 404 after deploy | `vercel.json` routes must match actual dist structure; see §1.5 for the correct config. `__root__.js` is NOT produced by Expo Router v5 static-server mode — each route in `vercel.json` must point to the corresponding pre-rendered HTML file in `dist/server/`. |
| API route returns 404 | Ensure the `vercel.json` route for `/api/secure-proxy` has `"dest"` set to `"/server/_expo/functions/api/secure-proxy+api.js"` — the filename must include the `+api.js` suffix exactly as Expo emits it. |

---

## 6. Post-Deployment Verification

### 6.1 Smoke test — site loads

- [ ] Open `https://app.yourdomain.com` in a private/incognito browser window
- [ ] Page renders (no blank white screen)
- [ ] Browser console: zero `CORS` errors
- [ ] Browser console: zero `401 Unauthorized` errors from Clerk

---

### 6.2 Test sign-up flow

- [ ] Navigate to your sign-up page (e.g. `https://app.yourdomain.com/sign-up`)
- [ ] Create a new account with a real email address
- [ ] Confirm email if required (check Clerk dashboard: **Users** tab shows new user)
- [ ] Redirected to authenticated route after sign-up ✅
- [ ] Sign out → sign back in → session persists ✅
- [ ] Hard refresh (`Cmd+Shift+R`) → still authenticated ✅ (Clerk cookie-based
      sessions survive refresh on web)

---

### 6.3 Test data persistence per account

- [ ] Sign in as User A → create a record (e.g. a note, post, etc.)
- [ ] Sign out → sign in as User B
- [ ] Confirm User B cannot see User A's record (RLS is enforced) ✅
- [ ] Sign back in as User A → record is still there ✅
- [ ] Open Supabase Dashboard → **Table Editor** → confirm row exists with correct
      `user_id` matching Clerk user ID ✅

---

### 6.4 Test API proxy route

# Replace with your actual production URL and a valid Clerk session token
curl -X POST https://app.yourdomain.com/api/secure-proxy \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <session_token_from_browser_devtools>" \
  -d '{"test": true}'

- [ ] Returns `200` (or expected response), not `404` or `500`
- [ ] Check Vercel **Functions** tab for invocation logs:
      `https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/functions`
- [ ] Confirm `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is accessible inside the function
      (add a temporary log and remove after test)
- [ ] Confirm unauthenticated requests are rejected (remove auth header → expect `401`)

---

### 6.5 Check Vercel Function logs

1. Go to **https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/logs**
2. In the filter bar at the top, set **Source** to **Function** (or filter by
   the route `/api/secure-proxy`) to isolate invocation logs from static asset
   requests.
3. Trigger a request to `https://app.yourdomain.com/api/secure-proxy` and watch
   the log stream in real time, or click any past invocation to expand its output.
4. Look for:
   - [ ] Function invoked (log line appears — confirms routing is working)
   - [ ] No `Missing environment variable` errors
   - [ ] No JWT / JWKS verification failures from Clerk
   - [ ] No Supabase connection errors
   - [ ] Response status `200` for authenticated requests

Common runtime errors and fixes:

| Runtime Error | Symptom | Fix |
|---------------|---------|-----|
| `CLERK_JWKS_URL` not configured or unreachable | `401` on all API calls; logs show JWT verification error or fetch failure against `clerk.*.lcl.dev` | Ensure `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is set to the `sk_live_*` value (not test key); live keys automatically use the correct JWKS endpoint. If you have manually set `CLERK_JWKS_URL`, confirm it points to `https://[your-clerk-frontend-api]/.well-known/jwks.json`. |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` missing | `500` from API route; logs show `Invalid API key` or `Missing Supabase credentials` | Add `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` as a Production env var in §3.3 and redeploy. Confirm it is NOT prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_`. |
| CORS error on API route | Browser console shows `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` blocked; preflight `OPTIONS` returns `404` or missing headers | Add an `OPTIONS` export to `app/api/secure-proxy+api.ts` that returns the correct `Access-Control-Allow-*` headers, and ensure `https://app.yourdomain.com` is in the allowed origins list. |
| `401` on API calls from the browser | Authenticated user gets `401`; Clerk session exists in browser | Confirm the client is sending `Authorization: Bearer <token>` using `await getToken()` from `useAuth()`. On web, Clerk does not automatically attach the header — you must fetch it and pass it explicitly. |
| Function cold-start timeout | First request after idle returns `504` | This is normal for serverless functions. If it is frequent, check that the function bundle is not excessively large (avoid importing heavy dependencies at the top level; use dynamic imports). |

- [ ] No persistent errors in function logs
- [ ] Authenticated POST returns expected response
- [ ] Unauthenticated POST returns `401`

---

### 6.6 Troubleshoot 404s

If pages or the API route return 404 after a successful build, work through the
following steps in order.

**Step 1 — Reproduce the dist structure locally**

Run the production build on your machine and inspect the output:

npx expo export --platform web

ls dist/client/_expo/static/js/web/
# → entry-*.js  (main bundle)  plus locale chunk files

ls "dist/server/(tabs)/"
# → index.html  explore.html  scheduler.html

ls dist/server/_expo/functions/api/
# → secure-proxy+api.js

ls dist/server/
# → (tabs)/  (auth)/  _expo/  _sitemap.html  +not-found.html

If any of these paths are missing, the issue is in the Expo build configuration,
not in Vercel routing. Check `web.output = "server"` in `app.json` (§1.4).

**Step 2 — Verify vercel.json routes match the actual dist structure**

Open `vercel.json` and for every `"dest"` value, confirm the referenced path
exists under `dist/`. Common mismatches:

- `"dest": "/server/_expo/functions/__root__.js"` — this file does not exist;
  delete any route using it
- `"dest": "/server/(tabs)/index.html"` — confirm the parentheses are present
  in the actual directory name (they are — Expo uses the route group folder name)
- `"dest": "/server/_expo/functions/api/secure-proxy+api.js"` — confirm the
  `+api.js` suffix is present exactly as shown; do not omit the `+`

**Step 3 — Check that client assets use the client/ prefix**

JS bundles are in `dist/client/`, not `dist/server/`. The route for
`/_expo/static/**` must point to `/client/_expo/static/$1`, not
`/server/_expo/static/$1`. If this is wrong the page HTML loads but the JS
bundle 404s, leaving a blank white screen with no visible error.

**Step 4 — Inspect the deployed file tree in the Vercel dashboard**

1. Go to **https://vercel.com/[team]/[project]/deployments**
2. Click the deployment in question
3. Click **Source** (top-right of the deployment detail page)
4. Browse the file tree to confirm the expected files were uploaded:
   - `client/_expo/static/js/web/entry-*.js`
   - `server/(tabs)/index.html`
   - `server/_expo/functions/api/secure-proxy+api.js`

If files are missing from the deployed source, the build did not produce them —
recheck the Expo build configuration and re-run locally.

**Step 5 — Use the browser Network tab to identify the exact failing URL**

1. Open Chrome DevTools → **Network** tab → check **Preserve log**
2. Navigate to the 404ing page
3. Find the request with status `404` and note the exact URL path
4. Cross-reference that path against your `vercel.json` routes array:
   - If the path matches a `"src"` pattern, check the `"dest"` value
   - If no `"src"` pattern matches, the request falls through to the catch-all
     (`+not-found.html`) — add an explicit route for that path in `vercel.json`

**Step 6 — Redeploy after every vercel.json change**

`vercel.json` route changes require a new deployment to take effect. After
editing, commit and push (or run `vercel --prod`) and wait for the new
deployment to become the production alias before retesting.

- [ ] Local `dist/` structure matches what `vercel.json` routes expect
- [ ] No route in `vercel.json` references `__root__.js`
- [ ] `/_expo/static/**` routes point to `client/`, not `server/`
- [ ] Every app page has an explicit route entry in `vercel.json`
- [ ] Deployed source tree in Vercel dashboard contains expected files
- [ ] Browser Network tab shows no unexpected 404 URLs after fixes

### CHG-036 — 2026-03-30 UTC
**Type:** FIX (Vercel 404 — vercel.json routing rewritten for actual Expo Router v5 dist structure)
**Files changed:**
- `vercel.json` — Complete rewrite: explicit routes for each pre-rendered HTML page derived from dist/server/_expo/routes.json namedRegex patterns; static assets routed via /client/ prefix; API route fixed to reference secure-proxy+api.js; catch-all → +not-found.html
- `app/(auth)/_layout.tsx` — Added authEnabled guard: when no Clerk key, render Stack directly without calling useAuth() (which requires ClerkProvider)
- `VERCEL_DEPLOY.md` — §1.5 rewritten with correct vercel.json; §1.6 smoke-test updated; §5.2 error table extended; §6.5 completed; §6.6 Troubleshoot-404s added
- `scripts/vercel-404-fix-batch.mjs` *(NEW)* — Batch API script that generated fixes

**Key decisions:**
- Keep `"output": "server"` in app.json; Expo Router v5 with server output uses pre-rendered HTML, not SSR on every request, so each page requires an explicit Vercel route rather than a single catch-all handler
- The routes.json manifest at dist/server/_expo/routes.json is the canonical source of truth for URL→file mapping; all vercel.json routes must be derived from its namedRegex patterns
- Root cause of 404s was twofold: catch-all dest pointed to `__root__.js` (file does not exist in Expo Router v5 dist output), and the API route dest omitted the `+api` suffix, referencing `secure-proxy.js` instead of `secure-proxy+api.js`

**Notes:**
- Tests still pass; lint clean
- A full redeploy is required to pick up vercel.json changes — a config-only change does not hot-reload on Vercel
- Any new pages added to the app must also receive a corresponding explicit entry in vercel.json routes until a dynamic manifest-driven build step is wired into the deploy pipeline
